title: Look-Away Pass
description: Advanced passers learn to look one way and pass the other, moving the defender's eyes before the pass to open a passing lane.

content.objective: Use the eyes and head to move a defender, then deliver an accurate pass to the other side with peripheral vision.
content.setup: Passer at the top; receivers at both wings; a defender in the middle.
instructions: The passer looks at the left wing and turns the head and shoulders that way.
The defender in the middle shifts toward the left wing.
Without turning the head back, the passer passes to the right wing with a one-hand push.
The receiver catches ready to shoot.
Mix: sometimes look and pass the same way to keep the defender honest.
coachingPoints: Sell it with the whole upper body.
Peripheral vision: know where the target is before looking away.
One-hand pass: it is quicker and harder to read.
commonMistakes: Looking away and throwing blind to nobody.
Telegraphing the real pass with the feet.
Using the look-away when the simple pass is open.
content.safety: Moderate pass speed; receivers keep hands up at all times.
progressions: Defender plays live and may jump passes.
Look-away on a drive and kick.
regressions: Receivers wave so the passer can see them peripherally.
variations: Look-away bounce pass to a cutter.
Look-away from the post to the perimeter.
successCriteria: Defender moves with the eyes on most reps.
Pass arrives on target to the far wing.
content.gameApplication: Defenders read the passer's eyes; a look-away turns that against them.
